- When sentiment is strongly positive (e.g., >0.7) and forecast spikes upward, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid overshoot.  
- If sentiment turns negative (e.g., <0.2) and forecast remains high, lower the forecast by 5–10% to reflect mean reversion.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if the last 3–5 days show strong downward momentum, adjust forecast downward by 2–5% to account for lag.  
- If forecast consistently overestimates true values by >3% over 3–5 days, apply a 3–5% downward bias to future forecasts.  
- When sentiment is volatile (alternating +/–0.3), reduce forecast smoothness and apply a 1–2% downward correction to avoid overfitting to short-term noise.
